summary.text: A rocket is a long flying vehicle whose engine speeds it up without taking in any of the air around it.
The engine makes thrust by throwing exhaust out at high speed, and the rocket carries all its own propellant, so it can fly in the vacuum of space.
Rockets for military and recreational uses date back to at least 13th-century China, and in the 20th century they became the technology behind the Space Age and the Moon landings.

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: Italian word for a bobbin or spool, after its shape

facts.label: Earliest known uses
facts.value: Military and recreational, at least 13th-century China

facts.label: Most common power
facts.value: Chemical rockets, burning fuel with an oxidizer

facts.label: Range gain
facts.value: Military rocket range rose from 100 to 2,000 yards

facts.label: Modern uses
facts.value: Fireworks, missiles, satellite launches, human spaceflight

items.prompt: A rocket is coasting far above the atmosphere, where there is no air to speak of. Why can its engine still speed it up?

options.label: It pushes off the thin traces of gas still floating around
It carries everything it burns, so it needs nothing from outside
It is pulled forward by the Moon's gravity
It uses sunlight as a surface to push against

items.explain: A rocket is fuelled entirely by propellant it carries and needs no oxygen from air, so it can fly in the vacuum of space.

items.prompt: A language historian explains where the name "rocket" came from. What is the link?

options.label: It copies an old German word for the roar of its exhaust
It honours a medieval Italian engineer who first built one
It comes from a Chinese word for an arrow of fire
It comes from an Italian word for a thread spool, matching its shape

items.explain: The name comes from the Italian rocchetta, meaning bobbin or little spindle, because the shape resembled the spool that held thread.

items.prompt: A designer wants a vehicle that can break free of Earth's pull and climb with no maximum altitude. What design feature does it need?

options.label: It needs more than one stage
It needs large wings to gain extra lift
It needs air-breathing engines for the climb
It needs one stage holding all its fuel

items.explain: Multistage rockets can reach escape velocity from Earth, and so can achieve unlimited maximum altitude.

items.prompt: A safety officer says a chemical rocket accident can be especially severe. What is the reason?

options.label: Their exhaust is always poisonous to anyone nearby
They burn hotter than any other kind of engine
They hold a great deal of energy in a form that releases easily
Their tanks are always packed with gunpowder

items.explain: Chemical rockets store a large amount of energy in an easily released form, so the consequences of accidents can be severe.

items.prompt: In the mid-1200s, rocket technology reached the Middle East and Europe. How did it get there?

options.label: It began in China, and Mongol invasions carried it west
It began in Europe, and travellers carried it east
It began in the Middle East, and ships carried it onward
It began in India, and British soldiers brought it over

items.explain: Gunpowder rockets evolved in medieval China, the Mongols adopted the technology, and it spread through their invasions to the Middle East and Europe.

items.prompt: What was new about the rockets built in the Kingdom of Mysore in the late 18th century?

options.label: They were the first to be fired in groups from launching platforms
They were the first rockets guided by an electric steering system
They were the first rockets to be built with several stages
They were the first successful rockets with an iron case

items.explain: The Mysorean rockets were the first successful iron-cased rockets.
